If a shared environmental factor (temperature, humidity, vibration) affects both systems, it would produce correlated baseline jitter and occasional spikes. Day 7 pendulum cluster and day 8 resonator cluster show elevated variance on the same calendar days, suggesting common causation. Thermal effects on pendulum length and resonator stiffness are mundane and well-established. However, baselines remain stable across 10 days (no obvious secular trend), which weakens pure drift but is consistent with cyclic or episodic coupling.
- [p=0.35] Independent measurement technique variance in each lab — Pendulum and resonator scatter independently if operator technique, phase-locking, or timing resolution differs between trials. This explains why outliers do not cluster temporally across labs: trial 46 (day 7 pendulum) and trial 49 (day 8 resonator) are 1 day apart but in different instruments. Each lab may have distinct sources of noise (reaction time in pendulum counting; frequency-lock stability in resonator). Does not require environmental coupling; is reproducible across repeated independent trials.
- [p=0.15] Instrumental calibration drift or micro-hysteresis undetected in baseline period — If either instrument has begun to drift on a timescale shorter than 10 days (e.g., elastic relaxation, solder creep, bearing wear), it would appear as scatter around a nominally stable mean rather than a clean trend. Weaker evidence because: (i) no unambiguous secular trend observed; (ii) if true, I should see widening scatter or systematic direction by day 10, which is not apparent; (iii) requires instrument defect, which is less parsimonious than measurement noise.

Scatter is real, irreducible, and unrelated to environmental or technique factors. This is a default null — it does not explain the pattern, only accepts it.
